name: Outlook Home Page

evidence.rationale: Outlook application updates remove or restrict the legacy Home Page feature used to load malicious content when a folder is accessed. The relationship depends on deploying the relevant Outlook security updates.
Applying the relevant Outlook updates removes or restricts the legacy Home Page functionality used to load malicious content when a folder is accessed.

Microsoft updates removed or restricted the legacy Outlook Home Page functionality used for persistence. Preventing obsolete Outlook versions from executing directly prevents continued access to older vulnerable implementations.

Host-based intrusion prevention capabilities can enforce Attack Surface Reduction rules that prevent Office applications from creating child processes or writing potentially malicious executable content to disk.
